title: Stater: Lion (obverse); Incuse Punches (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Greek, minted at Miletos (Ionia)
caption: This electrum stater from Miletos pairs a lion with incuse punches. Its metal is an alloy of gold and silver.

title: Stater: Barley (obverse); Barley, Incuse (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Greek, minted at Metapontion (South Italy)
caption: A silver stater from Metapontion shows barley on both faces, with the reverse design incuse.
sourceNote: Caption is limited to the museum’s title, date, medium and cultural attribution; no extended object description is supplied.

title: Tetradrachm: Head of Athena (obverse); Owl (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Greek, minted at Athens (Attica)
caption: Athena and her owl identify this Athenian silver tetradrachm. The letters ΑΘΕ on the reverse abbreviate the city’s name.

title: Stater: Baal (obverse); Head of Pharnabazos (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Iran, Achaemenid (550–330 BCE), minted at Tarsos (Kilikia)
caption: This silver stater was minted at Tarsos under the Achaemenid Empire. Its catalogued subjects are Baal and the head of Pharnabazos.
sourceNote: Caption is limited to the museum’s title, date, medium and cultural attribution; no extended object description is supplied.

title: Punch-Marked Coin
creator: Unrecorded maker; India, Rajasthan, Maurya period (322–185 BCE)
caption: This Indian silver coin belongs to a tradition of cutting metal to weight and marking it with punches. Each piece carried its own combination of symbols.

title: Tetradrachm: Head of Young Herakles (obverse); Zeus (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Greek, Macedonian, minted at Amphipolis (Macedonia), reign of Alexander III [The Great]
caption: The youthful Herakles wears a lion skin on the front of this coin, while Zeus sits on the reverse. Its inscription names Alexander.

title: Tetradrachm Coin of Demetrios I
creator: Unrecorded maker; Afghanistan, Bactria, Indo-Greek
caption: Demetrios I appears wearing an elephant scalp on this silver tetradrachm. Hercules occupies the reverse.

title: Octodrachm: Head of Arsinoe II (obverse); Double Cornucopia (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Greek, Ptolemaic, minted at Alexandreia (Egypt), reign of Ptolemy V Epiphanes or Ptolemy VI Philometor
caption: Arsinoe II wears a crown and veil on this gold octodrachm. A pair of cornucopias appears on its reverse.

title: Ring Money
creator: Unrecorded maker; England
caption: This piece of gold ring money was found at Norman Leighton in Warwickshire. The museum notes that ring money could be strung and carried on the body.

title: Knife Coin
creator: Unrecorded maker; China
caption: This bronze object is catalogued by The Met as a knife coin from China’s Han dynasty. Its elongated form differs from the round coins elsewhere in the collection.
sourceNote: The museum supplies the period Han dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE), but no narrower object date. sortYear 7 is the midpoint used only for gallery ordering.

title: Aureus: Bust of Claudius I (obverse); Triumphal Arch with Equestrian Statue and Trophies (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; England, Roman, Claudius I (41–54 CE)
caption: This gold aureus pairs a portrait of Claudius I with a triumphal arch, an equestrian statue and trophies. The museum dates it to 47–48 CE.

title: Coin
creator: Unrecorded maker; India, Mathura, Kushan period
caption: A gold coin from the reign of the Kushan ruler Havishka. It places a ruler’s portrait on the obverse and a deity on the reverse.

title: Drachm: Bust of Hormizd II (obverse); Fire altar with bust (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Iran, (minted), Sasanian Empire (224–651 CE), reign of Hormizd II (303–309)
caption: This silver drachm dates to the reign of Hormizd II. The museum identifies a royal bust on the obverse and a fire altar with a bust on the reverse.
sourceNote: Caption is limited to the museum’s title, date, medium and cultural attribution; no extended object description is supplied.

title: Coin of Chandragupta II
creator: Unrecorded maker; India, Chandragupta II, Gupta Period, late 4th-early 5th century
caption: This gold coin of Chandragupta II depicts an archer carrying a bow and arrow. Shri, the goddess of good fortune, sits on a lotus on the reverse.

title: Tremissis of Honorius
creator: Unrecorded maker; Byzantium, Ravenna, Byzantine period, late 4th-early 5th Century
caption: The museum identifies this gold coin as a tremissis of Honorius, minted at Ravenna. A tremissis was one third of a solidus in weight and value.

title: Drachm: Bust of Napki Malka (obverse): Fire Altar (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Hephtalite, minted in Afghanistan, reign of Napki Malka
caption: A silver drachm catalogued to the reign of Napki Malka in Afghanistan. Its two sides show a ruler’s bust and a fire altar.
sourceNote: Caption is limited to the museum’s title, date, medium and cultural attribution; no extended object description is supplied.

title: Solidus of Justinian I
creator: Unrecorded maker; Byzantium, Constantinople, Byzantine period
caption: This solidus represents Justinian I and was minted at Constantinople. The gold solidus was a standard denomination of Byzantine coinage.

title: Witmen Tremissis: Bust and Trident (obverse); Cross Fourchée (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; England, Anglo-Saxon, early 7th century
caption: This early seventh-century gold tremissis follows the Witmen type. It pairs a bust and trident with a forked cross.

title: Solidus with Heraclius and his Son Heraclius Constantine
creator: Unrecorded maker; Byzantium
caption: This gold solidus depicts Heraclius and his son Heraclius Constantine. Byzantine coins increasingly represented heirs and co-emperors alongside the ruler.

title: Nomisma with Nicephorus II Phocas
creator: Unrecorded maker; Byzantium
caption: This gold nomisma represents Nicephorus II Phocas. The museum dates it to about 963–969, during the century when the nomisma replaced the solidus as the standard gold coin.
